chunks: Al-Ḥusayn, from Al-Ḥasan, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has water with him during travel, but fears its scarcity. He said: "He performs tayammum with earth and preserves the water, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made both of them means of purification: water and earth."

key_terms.اَلسَّفَرِ: travel; the state in which the ruling is being applied
key_terms.اَلْمَاءُ: water; the usual means of ritual purification being conserved
key_terms.بِالصَّعِيدِ: with earth; the material used for tayammum
key_terms.طَهُورًا: a means of purification; something by which ritual purity is attained
key_terms.قِلَّتَهُ: its scarcity; fear that the available water will not be enough
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum; the dry ablution used in place of wudu or ghusl in specific circumstances
key_terms.يَسْتَبْقِي: he preserves; he keeps the water for need

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler perform tayammum if he has water but fears it will run out?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning tayammum when a traveler has some water but fears that it may become insufficient. Imam Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that one may perform tayammum and conserve the water, because both water and earth have been made valid means of taharah by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
